title: Kerr ring four-wave mixing
description: Four-wave mixing INSIDE a Kerr ring resonator (models/optical_field/ring_kerr.va): two WDM lasers exactly one FSR apart (5.964 GHz for this R = 2 mm, Q = 1.5e6 ring) pump adjacent resonances — 1 mW on mode 0 at 1310 nm, 1 mW on mode +1 at 1309.9659 nm. The five ring modes share the intracavity chi(3) Kerr nonlinearity (the modal Lugiato-Lefever equations, momentum matched), so the idler EMERGES in mode -1 at 1310.0341 nm where 2f_p - f_s lands exactly on a resonance, and the mixing cascades into modes +-2 — the first teeth of a Kerr comb growing on the OSA. All three waves are resonantly enhanced: the same chi(3) in the same 12.6 mm of straight waveguide converts ~1000x less (compare example 39). The drop-port time trace shows the 6 GHz beat of the circulating comb building up over the ~2 ns photon lifetime. examples/ring_fwm.py pins the physics: P_i ~ P_p^2*P_s, the Lorentzian-to-the-4th detuning collapse, dispersion (d2_hz) killing the conversion = ring phase matching, and every line against an independent ODE integration
